ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the circuit diagram, the ground symbol at the lower right serves as the reference ground. At the lower right there is a 6V power source, labeled with the left end as “+” and the right end as “-”; its right end is grounded, and its left end is connected to the bottom central node. On the left side there is a 12V power source, labeled with the upper end as “+” and the lower end as “-”; its lower end is connected to the bottom central node, and its upper end is connected to the top left node. The top left node is connected through a 2Ω resistor to the top central node; the top central node goes downward through a vertical 4Ω resistor to connect to the bottom central node; the top central node also goes right through a 4Ω resistor to the open-circuit endpoint A. Reasoning: The potential of the ground node is 0V. Since the right end of the 6V power source is the negative end and is grounded, and the left end is the positive end, the potential of the bottom central node is +6V. The lower end of the 12V power source is connected to the bottom central node and the upper end is the positive end, so the potential of the top left node is 6V + 12V = 18V. Since the end of the right-side 4Ω resistor leading to A is open-circuited, the branch current is 0, so there is no voltage drop across this resistor, and the potential at point A equals the potential of the top central node. Between the top left 18V node and the bottom central 6V node, the 2Ω resistor and the vertical 4Ω resistor are in series, and the current is (18V - 6V) / (2Ω + 4Ω) = 2A. The voltage drop across the 2Ω resistor is 2A × 2Ω = 4V, so the potential of the top central node is 18V - 4V = 14V. Therefore, the potential at point A is 14V.

method.method_draft: First identify the grounded node as 0 V. From the 6 V source polarity, set the bottom central node to +6 V. From the 12 V source polarity, set the upper left node to 6 V + 12 V = 18 V. The 2 Ω and vertical 4 Ω resistors form a series path between 18 V and 6 V, so the current is (18−6)/(2+4) = 2 A. The drop across the 2 Ω resistor is 4 V, giving the central top node as 18−4 = 14 V. Since A is connected through an open-ended 4 Ω resistor with zero current, its voltage is the same as the central top node: 14 V.
